newsitem.title: UK: Technicals point to brighter future for UK gilts.
newsitem.headline: Technicals point to brighter future for UK gilts.

text.p: The British Labour government's inaugural budget has taken the shine off the gilt market for the time being, with the September future in danger of skidding down to 112-25, technical analysts said on Thursday.
But longer term, the outlook is not as tarnished as the knee-jerk sell-off suggests, they added.
"What the budget has probably done is take the top off the gilt market for a couple of weeks at least," said David Wood, an independent technical analyst near London.
"But things are not quite so obviously bearish as everybody has been thinking."

Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown's maiden budget on Wednesday sent shivers through the gilt market as interest rate expectations were revised up. City analysts said the net 5.5 billion sterling fiscal tightening was not enough to quell rampant consumer spending, leaving monetary policy to take up the slack.
"What the market needs to do now, if we're going to keep the idea the upside can continue, is to hold 113-22/26," said Wood.
The gilt market ricocheted higher off a low of 113-25 on Wednesday and off 113-24 so far on Thursday.
By 1031 GMT, September gilts were down 16/32 on the day at 114-09. September short sterling was down 16 basis points at 92.82 and December was off 0.20 at 92.62, up from its 92.56 low earlier.
"But if we go down through 113-22 there's a real chance we'll get another big figure to the downside with a target of 112-25," said Wood.
Daily charts show the market hit a low of 112-25 on June 24. "We ought to see quite a lot of buying between 112-25 and 112-00," said Wood.
Jonathan York, futures broker at MeesPierson Derivatives in London, said the contract may cling to Wednesday's close of 113-30 in automated trade.
"It's a bit tricky," he said. "I suspect the market will hold at Wednesday's after-hours level. It may just run down to 113-20,22 to try to flush out any stops."
York said a drop through here could trigger a run down to 113-06. Daily charts show an open at 113-06 on June 20 and a close there on June 23.
Below the 112-00 handle, Wood put the next major buttress at the May 22 low of 111-30.
But he said conflicting signals meant the longer term outlook for the market was not as bleak.
He noted the British stock market had pulled back from early lows to hit a new all-time record high.

He said the positive tone in other major bond markets should also lend gilts a helping hand, as should the fact the September contract hit a new high at 115-05 on Wednesday, a technical signal to the upside.
But selling pressure around 114-12/18 on Thursday meant gilts would struggle to fight their way through there near term, said Wood.
"The contract's probably worth a sell at those levels," he said. Above 114-18 the contract may have a bash at breaking 115-05, he added.
York agreed. "It could go as high as Wednesday's 115-05 contract high," he said, adding resistance from 114-06 to 114-14 would kick in first.
Elizabeth Miller, technical analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London, said short sterling would probably retrace some of its early session losses.
"This morning we saw it back down towards 92.50 which is a big psychological support level and we've seen a little bit of a bounce," she said.
But she said the upside would be limited to around 92.67, a 50 percent retracement of Wednesday's losses and the high in trade so far.
A break below 92.50 would turn the outlook severely negative, she said.
